title: Killing resistant tumors with a click - Nature Biotechnology
text:
Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) represent a promising approach for cancer therapy, but their efficacy is hampered by the variable expression of target antigens in heterogeneous tumors. Writing in Nature, Cristina Simó and colleagues report a bioorthogonal ‘click’ chemistry strategy to generate antibody–ADC complexes showing enhanced antitumor activity in mouse tumor models.The authors conjugated US Food and Drug Administration–approved antibodies and ADCs targeting human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) and epidermal growth factor receptor 1 (EGFR) with the complementary click reagents trans-cyclooctene and tetrazine. HER2 and EGFR are both clinically validated targets expressed across many tumor types, and EGFR is a key driver of acquired tumor resistance. Live-cell imaging studies in cancer cell lines showed that the antibody click ligation increased antibody internalization and endolysosomal trafficking. Sequential administration of the complexes in mice demonstrated successful antibody click reactions in vivo.
